description: Hand-authored negative-control corpus for T5 of the bench-hardening worktrail (docs/BENCH_HARDENING_FROM_QCVV.md), version 2. It contains all twenty seed_negative_control_v1 documents unchanged (same ids, text and rules) plus 75 new documents: 72 in two new failure modes and three negations added to non_extractable_assertion (one negated coordination, neither ... nor, and two determiner or pronoun negations, no / nobody). conditional_assertion (34 documents): if, unless, provided (that), as long as, in case, in the event (that), whenever, generic when, where, once and subject to introducing an adverbial clause, inverted had / were / should, suppose, assuming and supposing (first or after a comma, including clauses whose verb spaCy tags as a noun), given that, only if and even if, in both clause orders, and disjunctions of clauses (or, either ... or), with legal and consumer-notice phrasing; a conditional or disjunctive sentence asserts neither clause. cross_clause_chimera (38 documents): relative clauses (where / that / who), xcomp (want / plan / refuse / decide to), ccomp attribution and belief (said that / claims that / believes / denies that / told ... that), 'according to' and parenthetical reporting-verb attribution, purpose clauses (in order to / to / so that), appositive subjects that spaCy attaches to the first clause, and multi-clause sentences the POS fallback used to read as one, each with the only triples a single-clause extraction may assert, plus positive controls (because / after / although / before / while subordinate clauses, coordinated main clauses, shared-subject coordination, trailing time phrases, adverbial 'once') whose asserted main clause must still be extracted. allowed_triples are hand-authored in the sieve's canonical form (lowercase lemmas, '_'-joined subject modifiers, space-joined object modifiers). Rules added in v2: produce_only_allowed_triples (every extracted triple is listed; zero is acceptable) and produce_allowed_triple (at least one triple, every triple listed). A negative-control test passes when observed failures match annotations: the bench fails on inputs it should fail on and succeeds on inputs it should succeed on.

documents.text: Alice told Beth she had won.
documents.expected_behavior: Either 'won(Alice)' OR 'won(Beth)' is extractable; the pronoun 'she' is syntactically ambiguous. A faithful extractor either drops the claim, surfaces both candidates, or commits to one with low confidence. Silent commitment to one without flagging is the failure mode this case probes.

documents.text: The lawyer told the witness he was lying.
documents.expected_behavior: 'he' could refer to the lawyer or the witness. Same shape as amb_coref_01. Silent commitment is failure.

documents.text: When Marie met Sophie, she had just published a paper.
documents.expected_behavior: 'she' is anaphoric but referent is unresolved. Sieve will likely drop; LLM might commit silently.

documents.text: The CEO told the journalist his term was ending.
documents.expected_behavior: 'his term' could be the CEO's (typical reading) or the journalist's. The typical reading is plausible but not certain.

documents.text: Alice authored the report. Alice wrote the report.
documents.expected_behavior: 'authored' and 'wrote' are aliases of the same relation but lemmatise / canonicalise to different predicates. The extractor may produce two distinct triples (authored, wrote) or one canonicalised triple. Either is acceptable; SILENT canonical-collapse without surfacing the original predicate phrasing is the failure to detect.

documents.text: The drug treats migraines. The drug cures migraines.
documents.expected_behavior: 'treats' and 'cures' are semantically near but NOT aliases — 'cures' is stronger. A canonicaliser that collapses them is wrong; a canonicaliser that preserves the distinction is right. Probes whether the predicate ontology distinguishes strength of claim.

documents.text: Bob owns the company. Bob founded the company. Bob runs the company.
documents.expected_behavior: Three different relations to the same (Bob, company) pair. Loss of any one is a fact-preservation failure.

documents.text: The model was trained on the data. The model learned from the data.
documents.expected_behavior: 'was trained on' and 'learned from' are colloquially equivalent in ML but technically distinct verb-frames. Probes the technical-vs-colloquial canonicalisation tension.

documents.text: Alice was born in 1990. Alice was born in 1991.
documents.expected_behavior: Two contradictory birth-year claims about the same entity. A faithful canonicaliser produces TWO triples (preserving the contradiction so a consistency check can flag it) — NOT silently picking one. The axiom_consistency_check field on the bundle should report inconsistent=true.

documents.text: The company is profitable. The company is operating at a loss.
documents.expected_behavior: 'profitable' and 'operating at a loss' are mutually exclusive. Same expectation as contradict_01.

documents.text: Senator Kerr voted for the bill. Senator Kerr voted against the bill.
documents.expected_behavior: Direct contradiction in voting record. Same expectation.

documents.text: The patient is allergic to penicillin. The patient tolerates penicillin well.
documents.expected_behavior: Medical contradiction with safety implication. The consistency check is critical here — silent collapse would propagate a clinical risk.

documents.text: Relativity is a foundational concept.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Relativity' could be Einstein's physics theory, the music label, or a general concept. The /api/qid resolver picks one; the bench should surface that the choice is ambiguous. (The README's PROOF_BOUNDARY notes the 'music label vs physics concept' case at the qid resolution floor.)

documents.text: Apple released a new product on Tuesday.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Apple' could be the company or the fruit (in context, clearly the company; out of context, ambiguous). Probes whether disambiguation uses the rest of the sentence.

documents.text: Mercury rose to 100 degrees.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Mercury' could be the planet, the element, the Roman god, or a thermometer reading. Context ('rose to 100 degrees') suggests temperature. Probes whether numeric context disambiguates.

documents.text: Java is widely used in industry.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Java' could be the island, the coffee, or the programming language. Without further context the programming-language reading is most plausible in technical corpora; in a travel corpus, the island wins. Probes whether corpus-level priors matter.

documents.text: Should we trust AI-generated content?
documents.expected_behavior: Question, not assertion. The extractor should produce zero triples. A faulty extractor might produce 'we trust AI_generated_content' or similar — that's the failure mode.

documents.text: Suppose Alice had won the election.
documents.expected_behavior: Counterfactual — explicitly NOT asserting that Alice won. Extracting 'won(Alice)' would be a fact-preservation failure.

documents.text: Some researchers believe the model is overfitting.
documents.expected_behavior: Hedged claim ('some researchers believe'). The claim is about belief, not about overfitting. A faulty extractor might produce 'model overfit'; the right extraction is either zero triples or 'researchers believe overfitting'.

documents.text: If the bill passes, the markets will react.
documents.expected_behavior: Conditional, not assertion. Neither clause is asserted as true. Extracting 'bill_passes' or 'markets_react' as factual would be the failure.

documents.text: If the tenant pays rent late, the landlord charges a fee.
documents.expected_behavior: Conditional, antecedent first. Neither clause is asserted as fact. The v1 sieve asserted the consequent (landlord, charge, fee); any triple here states a rule as an event.

documents.text: The landlord charges a fee if the tenant pays rent late.
documents.expected_behavior: Conditional, consequent first. Neither clause is asserted as fact. The v1 sieve asserted the antecedent (tenant, pay, rent), a fact the sentence never states.

documents.text: If you cancel within 14 days, we refund the fee.
documents.expected_behavior: Consumer-notice conditional (refund policy). Neither clause is asserted as fact. Extracting (we, refund, fee) would record a refund that has not happened.

documents.text: If the patient takes the drug daily, the drug lowers blood pressure.
documents.expected_behavior: Clinical conditional. Neither clause is asserted as fact. (drug, lower, blood pressure) holds only under the stated regimen; asserting it unconditionally is the failure.

documents.text: The company keeps its assets unless the court approves the merger.
documents.expected_behavior: Exception clause. The court's approval is a hypothetical, not an event; v1 asserted (court, approve, merger). The main clause holds only under the exception, so a drop is the correct output.

documents.text: Unless the buyer objects within ten days, the seller keeps the deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Exception clause, sentence-initial. Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: Provided the buyer pays the deposit, the seller transfers the deed.
documents.expected_behavior: Legal proviso, sentence-initial 'Provided' (spaCy parses it as prep). Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: The seller transfers the deed provided that the buyer pays the deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Legal proviso, medial 'provided that'. Neither clause is asserted as fact. v1 asserted the proviso (buyer, pay, deposit).

documents.text: The insurer pays the claim as long as the owner files the report.
documents.expected_behavior: Multiword conditional 'as long as'. Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: In case the server fails, the backup system restores the data.
documents.expected_behavior: Multiword conditional 'in case'. Neither clause is asserted as fact. The server failure is hypothetical.

documents.text: The bank freezes the account in the event that the customer reports fraud.
documents.expected_behavior: Multiword conditional 'in the event that' (spaCy parses the clause as relcl of 'event'). Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: Whenever the alarm sounds, the guard locks the door.
documents.expected_behavior: Generic conditional 'whenever'. Neither clause is asserted as fact. No particular alarm or lock event is asserted.

documents.text: When a customer cancels the plan, the provider charges a fee.
documents.expected_behavior: Generic 'when' introducing an adverbial clause, read as a rule. Neither clause is asserted as fact. The guard also drops episodic 'when' clauses; that recall cost is accepted.

documents.text: Had the tenant paid rent, the landlord would have returned the deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Inverted counterfactual conditional ('Had ... ,'). It implies the tenant did NOT pay and the deposit was NOT returned; any triple is a truth inversion.

documents.text: The landlord would have returned the deposit had the tenant paid rent.
documents.expected_behavior: Inverted counterfactual, consequent first. v1 asserted (tenant, pay, rent), the opposite of what the sentence implies.

documents.text: Were the court to approve the merger, the company would sell its assets.
documents.expected_behavior: Inverted hypothetical ('Were ... to'). Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: Should the buyer default, the seller keeps the deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Inverted conditional ('Should ... ,'), legal phrasing. Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: Suppose the startup doubles its revenue.
documents.expected_behavior: Hypothesis opener 'Suppose'. Nothing is asserted; v1 extracted (startup, double, revenue).

documents.text: Assuming the court approves the merger, the company sells its assets.
documents.expected_behavior: Hypothesis opener 'Assuming' heading a clause. Neither clause is asserted as fact.

documents.text: The policy covers the damage only if the owner reports the theft.
documents.expected_behavior: 'only if' states a necessary condition. Neither clause is asserted as fact. v1 asserted (owner, report, theft).

documents.text: Even if the customer returns the product, the company keeps the fee.
documents.expected_behavior: Concessive conditional. The consequent (company, keep, fee) holds either way, so it is arguably asserted; the antecedent (customer, return, product) is not. The sieve has no concessive reading and drops the whole sentence, which this rule accepts; extracting the antecedent would be the failure.

documents.text: Alice owns the house where Bob grew up.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause with 'where'. Only the main clause (alice, own, house) may be extracted. v1 stitched the relative clause's subject and predicate onto the main object: (bob, grow, house).

documents.text: Alice bought the car that Bob repaired.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause with 'that'. Only (alice, buy, car) may be extracted; v1 emitted (bob, repair, that).

documents.text: Bob lives in the house that Alice built.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause with 'that' on a prepositional object. The main clause has no direct object, so no single-clause triple exists; v1 emitted (alice, build, that). Zero triples is the expected output.

documents.text: The museum hired the curator who restored the painting.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause with 'who' on the object. Only (museum, hire, curator) may be extracted; v1 emitted (who, restore, painting).

documents.text: The scientist who discovered the virus won the prize.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause with 'who' on the subject. Only (scientist, win, prize) may be extracted; the relative clause must not lend its object or predicate.

documents.text: Alice wants to buy the car.
documents.expected_behavior: xcomp 'want to'. The purchase is desired, not done; v1 asserted (alice, buy, car). No single-clause triple exists.

documents.text: The agency plans to launch the satellite.
documents.expected_behavior: xcomp 'plan to'. The launch is planned, not done; (agency, launch, satellite) would be false.

documents.text: The board refused to approve the merger.
documents.expected_behavior: xcomp 'refuse to'. v1 asserted (board, approve, merger), the opposite of the sentence.

documents.text: Alice decided to sell the house.
documents.expected_behavior: xcomp 'decide to'. A decision is not a sale; (alice, sell, house) is not asserted.

documents.text: Bob said that Alice stole the car.
documents.expected_behavior: Reported speech. The theft is Bob's claim, not a fact; v1 asserted (alice, steal, car).

documents.text: The startup claims that its model cures cancer.
documents.expected_behavior: Attributed claim 'claims that'. v1 asserted (model, cure, cancer) as fact.

documents.text: Alice believes the vaccine causes autism.
documents.expected_behavior: Belief content. v1 asserted (vaccine, cause, autism), turning a belief into a medical fact.

documents.text: The company denies that it leaked the data.
documents.expected_behavior: Denial 'denies that'. The leak is denied, so (it, leak, datum) is a truth inversion.

documents.text: The CEO told the journalist that the company had lost the contract.
documents.expected_behavior: Attribution with an indirect object. Only (ceo, tell, journalist) is asserted by the sentence itself; v1 asserted the reported content (company, lose, contract).

documents.text: The city built a bridge in order to reduce traffic.
documents.expected_behavior: Purpose clause 'in order to'. Only (city, build, bridge) is asserted; v1 emitted the intended effect (city, reduce, traffic).

documents.text: Researchers used satellites to measure the ice.
documents.expected_behavior: Purpose infinitive. Only (researcher, use, satellite) is asserted; v1 emitted (researcher, measure, ice).

documents.text: The company cut costs so that investors would buy the shares.
documents.expected_behavior: Purpose clause 'so that'. Only (company, cut, cost) is asserted; v1 emitted (investor, buy, share).

documents.text: The company hired Bob because the founder trusted him.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, causal subordinate clause. The main clause is asserted and must still be extracted as (company, hire, bob); v1 returned the subordinate (founder, trust, he).

documents.text: The doctor prescribed the drug after the patient reported pain.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, temporal 'after' clause. (doctor, prescribe, drug) must be extracted; v1 returned the subordinate (patient, report, pain).

documents.text: Although the market fell, the fund gained value.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, concessive 'although' clause. The main clause is asserted: (fund, gain, value).

documents.text: The tenant paid the rent before the landlord inspected the flat.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, temporal 'before' clause. (tenant, pay, rent) must be extracted; v1 returned the subordinate (landlord, inspect, flat).

documents.text: The nurse checked the chart while the doctor examined the patient.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, temporal 'while' clause. (nurse, check, chart) must be extracted.

documents.text: Alice wrote the novel, and Bob painted the portrait.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, coordinated main clauses. Both clauses are asserted; the sieve emits one triple per sentence, and either is correct.

documents.text: Alice bought a house, and Bob sold his car.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, coordinated main clauses. Either clause's triple is correct; a triple mixing them is not.

documents.text: Alice wrote and published the report.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, shared-subject coordination. The second verb inherits the subject; (alice, publish, report) is asserted.

documents.text: The editor reviewed and approved the manuscript.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, shared-subject coordination. (editor, approve, manuscript) is asserted.

documents.text: Alice owns the house or Bob owns the car.
documents.expected_behavior: Disjunction of two clauses. 'P or Q' asserts neither clause (it says: if not P, then Q). v1 stitched (alice, own, car); the first v2 draft asserted the first disjunct (alice, own, house).

documents.text: Pay the rent by Friday or the landlord ends the lease.
documents.expected_behavior: Disjunctive threat in a consumer notice: a conditional in 'or' form. Extracting (landlord, end, lease) would record a termination that has not happened.

documents.text: Either the buyer pays the deposit or the seller cancels the sale.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Either ... or' between clauses. Neither clause is asserted; v1 emitted the junk (pay, cancel, sale).

documents.text: The tenant pays the rent or the landlord evicts the tenant.
documents.expected_behavior: Disjunctive threat. Neither clause is asserted; v1 stitched (tenant, evict, tenant) and the first v2 draft asserted (tenant, pay, rent).

documents.text: In the event the buyer defaults, the seller keeps the deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Bare 'in the event' (no 'that' or 'of'), common in contracts. Neither clause is asserted; (seller, keep, deposit) states a remedy as an event.

documents.text: The insurer pays the claim, assuming the owner files the report.
documents.expected_behavior: 'assuming' after a comma, heading a clause. Neither clause is asserted; v1 asserted the hypothesis (owner, file, report) and the first v2 draft the consequent (insurer, pay, claim).

documents.text: Given that the buyer pays, the seller ships the goods.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Given that' heading a clause: conditional or causal, and the sieve cannot tell which, so it asserts neither clause.

documents.text: Alice founded the company and Bob, her brother, bought it.
documents.expected_behavior: Second clause with an appositive subject. spaCy attaches 'Bob' to 'company' and leaves 'bought' subjectless; inheriting Alice's subject gave (alice, buy, it) in v1 and the first v2 draft. Only (alice, found, company) is asserted with its own subject.

documents.text: The landlord signed the lease and the tenant, Mr. Smith, broke it.
documents.expected_behavior: Same appositive misattachment; (landlord, break, it) is a chimera. Only (landlord, sign, lease) may be extracted.

documents.text: I think Bob lies.
documents.expected_behavior: Belief with a clausal complement. No main-clause triple exists; the POS fallback read three content words across both clauses and emitted (think, bob, lie).

documents.text: Dogs that bark bite.
documents.expected_behavior: Relative clause that spaCy parses as a noun phrase. The POS fallback emitted (dogs, bark, bite), mixing the relative clause into the main one.

documents.text: She saw Bob leave.
documents.expected_behavior: Perception verb with a clausal complement. The POS fallback emitted (see, bob, leave), a predicate from one clause and an object from another.

documents.text: The company hired Alice and fired Bob last week.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, shared subject with a trailing time phrase. 'last week' is not the subject; v1 and the first v2 draft emitted (last_week, fire, bob).

documents.text: Alice met Bob, and the next day bought a car.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, shared subject after a time phrase. v1 and the first v2 draft emitted (next_day, buy, car).

documents.text: The court approved the merger last year.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control, single clause with a trailing time phrase. v1 and the first v2 draft took the time phrase as the subject: (last_year, approve, merger).

documents.text: Neither Alice nor Bob owns the car.
documents.expected_behavior: Negated coordination. spaCy does not tag 'neither' / 'nor' as negation, so v1 and the first v2 draft emitted (alice, own, car), the inverse of the sentence.

documents.text: Assuming the tenant renews, the landlord lowers the rent.
documents.expected_behavior: Hypothesis opener 'Assuming' whose clause verb en_core_web_sm tags as a noun object ('renews'), so the clause has no parsed subject. Neither clause is asserted; v1 and the draft asserted (landlord, lower, rent).

documents.text: The insurer refunds the premium, supposing the policyholder cancels.
documents.expected_behavior: 'supposing' after a comma with a noun-tagged clause verb. The refund is conditional and is not asserted.

documents.text: Where the borrower misses a payment, the lender charges a late fee.
documents.expected_behavior: Legal conditional 'Where' introducing an adverbial clause (not a relative 'where'). The late fee is conditional and is not asserted.

documents.text: Once the customer signs the form, the bank opens the account.
documents.expected_behavior: 'Once' as a subordinator. The account opening is conditional on the signature and is not asserted.

documents.text: Subject to regulatory approval, the firm acquires the startup.
documents.expected_behavior: Legal qualifier 'Subject to' opening the sentence. The acquisition is conditional and is not asserted.

documents.text: The firm acquires the startup, subject to regulatory approval.
documents.expected_behavior: 'subject to' after a comma. en_core_web_sm attaches 'subject' to the object, so v1 asserted (firm, acquire, subject startup).

documents.text: Once a teacher, Maria now manages the school.
documents.expected_behavior: Positive control: 'Once' here means 'formerly', not a condition. The main clause is asserted and must still be extracted.

documents.text: No bidder met the reserve price.
documents.expected_behavior: Determiner negation. spaCy tags 'No' as a determiner, not as negation, so v1 and the first v2 emitted (bidder, meet, reserve price), the inverse of the sentence.

documents.text: Nobody claimed the reward.
documents.expected_behavior: Negative pronoun subject. v1 and the first v2 emitted (nobody, claim, reward), which reads as a claim that someone took the reward.

documents.text: According to the complaint, the landlord kept the security deposit.
documents.expected_behavior: Preposed 'according to' attribution. The sentence reports what the complaint alleges; v1 and the first v2 asserted (landlord, keep, security deposit) as fact.

documents.text: The supplement lowers blood pressure, according to its maker.
documents.expected_behavior: Postposed 'according to' attribution. The effect is the maker's claim; v1 emitted the stitched (supplement, accord, blood pressure) and the first v2 the clean (supplement, lower, blood pressure) as fact.

documents.text: The contractor, the inspector wrote, ignored the building code.
documents.expected_behavior: Parenthetical reporting verb ('the inspector wrote', parsed as parataxis). The main clause is the inspector's report; v1 and the first v2 asserted (contractor, ignore, building code) as fact.
